q: 202. The time corresponding to minimum total project cost is
options: between normal time and crash time
explain: The optimum duration (minimum total cost point) usually lies between the normal time and crash time, at the intersection of direct and indirect cost curves.

q: 203. The cost slope is defined as
options: (crash cost - normal cost)/(normal time - crash time)
explain: Cost slope is calculated as (crash cost - normal cost) divided by (normal time - crash time), giving cost increase per unit time reduction.

q: 204. Quality control is done by
explain: Quality control is achieved through measurement of the work performed against specified standards.

q: 205. The reduction in project time normally results in
options: decreasing the direct cost and increasing indirect cost
increasing the direct cost and decreasing the indirect cost
increasing the direct cost and indirect cost both
decreasing the direct cost and indirect cost both
explain: Reducing project time (crashing) increases direct cost (extra resources needed) while decreasing indirect cost (shorter overhead duration).

q: 206. Time and progress chart of a construction is also known as
explain: A time-and-progress chart is essentially a bar/Gantt chart and can relate to CPM-based tracking, so all of the above apply.

q: 207. The object of technical planning is
options: initiating the procurement action of resources
explain: Technical planning covers preparing specifications, estimates, and initiating procurement of resources - all these objectives.

q: 208. A muster roll is:
options: attendance sheet of temporary workers for remuneration
inventory list of equipment and list of people on the site
list of jobs the workers must do on site
several drawing sheets of site rolled in a bundle
explain: A muster roll is the attendance record of temporary/casual workers used to calculate their wages/remuneration.

q: 209. Slack time in PERT analysis
options: can never be greater than zero
is always zero for critical activities
can never be less than zero
explain: Critical activities/events in PERT always have zero slack, as they lie directly on the critical path with no room for delay.

q: 210. Petty contract is:
options: work entrusted to a contractor without any restrictions
contract wholly owned by a single staff
contract selected as the best one
a contract of small amount and volume to be fully handled by a staff
explain: A petty contract involves a small amount/volume of work that can be fully managed and handled by a single designated staff member.

q: 211. Amount required to be deposited by contractor while submitting tender is
explain: Earnest money is the amount a contractor deposits along with the tender submission as a guarantee of serious intent.

q: 212. In the construction industry arbitration method is used for:
explain: Arbitration is a dispute resolution method used during contract execution, not related to tender inviting, opening, or awarding stages - hence none of the above.

q: 213. Types of organization used in construction industry is:
explain: Per the answer key, 'effective organization' is listed as the correct type, though line, line-staff, and functional organizations are the more standard classifications used in construction.

q: 214. Updating of schedule is carried out in a project
options: to assign new target date against the planned date
to reflect remedial actions for correction of deviations
explain: Schedule updating serves multiple purposes: accommodating changes, resetting target dates, and reflecting corrective actions - all of the above.

q: 215. The document announcing to prospective bidders that the owner is ready to receive bids is called
explain: A 'notice to bidders' (or tender notice) is the document that announces the owner's readiness to receive bids from prospective bidders.

q: 216. Which of the following is not a reason for establishing good occupational health and safety standard?
explain: Religious grounds are not a recognized rationale for occupational health and safety standards, unlike economic, legal, and moral reasons.

q: 217. Critical Path method (CPM) in construction management required single time estimates whereas programme evaluation and Review Technique (PERT) requires:
explain: PERT requires three (triple) time estimates - optimistic, most likely, and pessimistic - unlike CPM's single estimate.

q: 218. If the variation amount is in between 10% to15% of the original contract value then approval of the variation of cost is done by:
explain: For a variation of 10-15% of contract value, approval authority can rest with the project manager, site in-charge, or department head depending on the delegated authority level - so all of the above.

q: 219. FIDIC is
explain: FIDIC stands for the International Federation of Consulting Engineers, known for its standard contract forms.

q: 220. The amount provided in the estimate and bill of quantities for some specialized works to be done by the specialist firm, whose details are not known at the time of preparing estimates is called
explain: A provisional sum is an amount included in the estimate for specialized works whose exact scope/details are not known at estimate preparation time.

q: 221. Responsibility of civil Engineer is
explain: A civil engineer's responsibilities span supervision, quality control, and BOQ preparation - all of the above.

q: 222. Construction activities at site are associated with the management of
explain: Site construction activities require coordinated management of manpower, material, and machinery/equipment - all of the above.

q: 223. Muster roll consists of
explain: A muster roll is specifically an attendance record of workers, not a list of cost, material, or equipment - hence none of above.

q: 224. The report prepared at the end of finishing a construction job is called:
explain: A completion report is prepared upon finishing a construction job, summarizing the work executed.

q: 225. A set of documents submitted by a contractor to a project office with a description of works or goods to be provided and the proposed price is known as
explain: A tender is the set of documents submitted by a contractor describing proposed works/goods and their prices.

q: 226. Donor funded project are based on
explain: Donor-funded projects consider government priorities, user needs, and economic viability (IRR) - all of these factors.

q: 227. In Nepal, which of the following Act contains the provisions on health and safety of the workers?
explain: In Nepal, the Labour Act contains provisions specifically related to the health and safety of workers.

q: 228. As per the financial regulation minimum time required for tender notice is for NCB contract:
explain: Financial regulations stipulate a minimum of 30 days for tender notice period for National Competitive Bidding (NCB) contracts.

q: 229. Technology is the
options: study of machines and their operation
study of behaviour of men and machines
explain: Technology, by definition, is the study/application of techniques and methods for performing tasks.

q: 230. A company or organization (the promoter, client or employer) wishing to obtain goods or services will first
explain: The procurement process begins with the client specifying their requirements before proceeding to estimation and sourcing.

q: 231. Consulting works worth more than 10 crore NRS should be procured on the basis of
options: International level request for EOI and RFP
explain: For high-value consulting contracts exceeding NRS 10 crore, procurement follows an international-level Request for Proposal process.

q: 232. Which of the following mode of selection is related to procurement of goods?
explain: CBS (Cost-Based Selection) is the mode typically associated with procurement of goods, distinct from consultant selection methods like QCBS/QBS.

q: 233. Which of the following method of procurement isn't applicable for material management?
explain: QCBS (Quality and Cost Based Selection) is used for consultant selection, not applicable for material/goods procurement.

q: 234. Contract completion report is a summary of
options: Financial summary of payments including variation orders and claims
explain: A contract completion report summarizes contract description, financial payment details, and the taking-over certificate - all of the above.

q: 235. At a work site, statistical quality control of concrete means
options: Measurement of risks to eliminate failures
Applying the theory of probability to sample testing or inspection
Reduction in wastage of inspection costs
Reduction in costs for the removal of defects
explain: Statistical quality control applies probability theory to sample testing/inspection results to assess and control concrete quality.

q: 236. In time-cost optimization of a project, crashing is done.
options: on all the activities lying on the critical path
only on activities lying on the orginal critical path and having flatter cost slopes
on original critical activities and those that become critical at any stage of crashing in the order of ascending cost slope
explain: Crashing in time-cost optimization is applied progressively to critical activities (including newly critical ones as crashing proceeds), always in ascending order of cost slope.

q: 237. The amount required to be deposited by a contractor while submitting a tender is known as
explain: The amount deposited with tender submission is termed earnest money deposit, serving as a bid guarantee.

q: 238. Which of the following excavators is most suitable for digging under water?
explain: A clam shell excavator, with its grab-bucket mechanism, is best suited for digging in submerged/underwater conditions.

q: 239. Which of the following earth moving machines has the shortest cycle time?
explain: The dipper shovel, being a direct digging and loading machine, has the shortest operational cycle time among the listed excavators.

q: 240. Interfering float is the difference between
explain: Interfering float is defined as the difference between total float and free float of an activity.

q: 241. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: The activity which consumes maximum time, is called a node
The activity is the time consuming part of a project
The beginning and end of a job, are called events
Logically and sequentially connected activities and events form a network
explain: This statement is incorrect - a 'node' represents an event (start/end point), not the activity consuming maximum time.

q: 242. The time by which activity completion time can be delayed without affecting the start of succeeding activities, is known as:
explain: Free float specifically measures delay possible in an activity without affecting the succeeding activity's start.

q: 243. In a PERT network, the earliest (activity) start time is the
options: Earliest time that an activity can be finished without delaying the entire project.
Latest time that an activity can be started without delaying the entire project.
Earliest time that an activity can start without violation of precedence requirements.
Latest time that an activity can be finished without delaying the entire project.
explain: Earliest start time is defined as the earliest possible time an activity can begin, respecting all preceding activity dependencies.

q: 244. Which of the following is one of the assumptions of PERT?
options: Total project completion time follows a normal probability distribution.
Activity times are dependent and correlated.
Project completion time follows a skewed chi-square distribution.
Activity times are known with certainty.
explain: PERT assumes that the sum of many independent activity durations along the critical path leads to an overall project completion time following a normal distribution (by central limit theorem).

q: 245.  An important assumption in PERT calculations is:
explain: PERT assumes individual activity times are statistically independent of each other, which allows summing their variances along the critical path.

q: 246. Which is/are features of PERT/CPM?
options: An estimate of how long a project will take.
A graphical display of project activities.
explain: PERT/CPM techniques provide time estimates, graphical network displays, and identify critical activities - all of the above.

q: 247. An event is indicated on the network by a number enclosed in
explain: Events are conventionally represented on network diagrams by numbers enclosed within circles (nodes).

q: 248. Time and progress chart of a construction, is also known as
explain: A time-and-progress chart is related to bar/Gantt charts and can also connect to milestone tracking - so all the above apply.

q: 249. In the given figure, the network of a project represents
options: activity of an excavation of a footing
activity of an excavation which starts at event No. 1 and ends at even No. 2
activity of excavation which takes 8 units of time
explain: The figure shows the excavation activity between events 1 and 2 labeled with duration '8', indicating it takes 8 units of time to complete.

q: 250. Grader is used mainly for
explain: A motor grader is primarily used for shaping and trimming earth surfaces to the required grade/profile.

q: 251. Completion of an activity on CPM network diagram, is generally known
explain: The completion point of an activity is called an event, represented as a node/connector point - all the above terms apply.

q: 252. Select the correct statement.
options: Activity arrows in a CPM network are drawn to scale
The tail of an arrow represents the finish of an activity
Arrow head represents the start of an activity
explain: None of the statements is correct: arrows are not to scale, tail is the start (not finish), and arrowhead is the finish (not start).

q: 253. In the network shown in Fig., the concurrent and preceding activities corresponding to activity 2-4 are respectively
explain: From the given network, activity 2-3 is concurrent with 2-4, and 1-2 precedes both, matching answer key option b.

q: 254. A Milestone chart
options: shows the interdependencies of various jobs
depicts the delay of jobs, if any
points outgoing ahead of schedule of jobs, if any
explain: A milestone chart does not show interdependencies between jobs (that's a network diagram's function), so per the answer key, none of these accurately describes it fully.

q: 255. Quality control ensures that the physical works conforms to
options: Strength specified in the contract document
Standard specified in the contract document
explain: Quality control ensures the executed work conforms to the standards specified in the contract document.

q: 256. In the initial stage of the project the probability of completing the project is
explain: At the initial stage of a project, uncertainty is highest and progress is minimal, so the probability of on-time completion assessment tends to be low.

q: 257. Controlling the changes in the project may affect
explain: Change control impacts project progress, costs, and scope simultaneously - all of the above.

q: 258. The process of incorporating changes and rescheduling or replanning is called
explain: Updating is the process of incorporating changes and rescheduling/replanning the project based on actual progress.

q: 259. The constraints in case of resource smoothening operation would be
options: both resources and project duration time
explain: In resource smoothening, the project duration is kept fixed (as the constraint) while resource allocation is adjusted within non-critical activities' float.

q: 260. The independent float affects only
explain: Independent float pertains solely to the specific activity in question, without any bearing on preceding or succeeding activities.

q: 261. Which of the following method of procurement is not applicable for material management?
explain: Cost and Quality Based Selection (QCBS) is a consultant-selection method, not applicable to material/goods procurement.

q: 262. An event is:
options: a definite position of an activity
explain: An event represents the terminal points (start or end nodes) of an activity in a network diagram.

q: 263. Choose the correct statement from the following:
explain: PERT is indeed event-oriented, making this the correct statement among the options.

q: 264. Project maintenance is:
explain: Project/facility maintenance continues throughout the operational life of the project as an ongoing process.

q: 265. Project control begins early in the project with planning and ends late in the project with
explain: Project control spans from early planning through to a final post-implementation review at project closeout.

q: 266. The time by which activity completion time can be delayed without affecting the start of succeeding activities is known as:
explain: Free float specifically defines the permissible delay in an activity that does not affect the succeeding activity's start time.

q: 267. If the scheduled completion time of a project is more than the earliest expected time for completion of the project, then the probability of completion of the project within the scheduled completion time will be
explain: If the scheduled time exceeds the expected (mean) time, the project has a higher-than-average chance of completion within schedule, i.e., more than 50%.

q: 268. What a variation order may not necessarily contain?
explain: A variation order documents changes in quantities, rates, and new BOQ items, but does not necessarily specify overall project budget provisions.
